syllabusTopics: Biomolecules: Introduction and functions of carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, minerals, enzymes and water
Cell: Introduction of cell, concepts of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells

Detail structure of eukaryotic cells: cell wall, cell membrane, mitochondria, plastids, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi bodies, lysosomes, ribosomes, nucleus, chromosomes, cilia, flagella and cell inclusions
Cell division: Concept of cell cycle, types of cell division (amitosis, mitosis and meiosis) and significances

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Ecology scales from organism to population, community and ecosystem. A niche is a role, a habitat an address. Food chains pass on about ten percent of the energy at each step, which is why they stay short. Ponds and forests differ in their producers and share that energy rule.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
A population is the members of one species in a place. A community is the populations living together. An ecosystem adds the physical surroundings.
A niche is the role: what the organism eats, when it is active, and which conditions it tolerates. Two species do not keep identical niches for long.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: A community does not include the climate. An ecosystem does.  ·  Ten percent transfer is a loss, not a gain, at each step.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A keystone predator (e.g., sea otters) maintains balanced predator-prey dynamics.  ·  Primary succession begins on bare rock or volcanic ash; secondary succession follows disturbances like fire or flooding.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Biotic factors are the living influences. Abiotic factors are light, temperature, water, soil and salinity.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Distinguish between biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) factors.  ·  Understand the difference between population density and carrying capacity.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Food webs: interconnected feeding relationships between producers, consumers, and decomposers  ·  Energy flow: energy transfers through trophic levels (producers → herbivores → carnivores)  ·  Biomass: total mass of living organisms in an ecosystem  ·  Carrying capacity: maximum population size an environment can sustain

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Food chains and food webs illustrate energy transfer and nutrient cycling.  ·  Competition, predation, and mutualism shape species interactions.  ·  Ecosystems can be classified by location (terrestrial, aquatic, marine) or by productivity level.  ·  Population, community, ecosystem.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: How do keystone species influence ecosystem structure?  ·  Explain primary vs secondary ecological succession.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Learn about ecological succession stages (primary vs secondary).

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: An ecosystem includes → A  ·  Energy reaching the next trophic level is about → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: A food chain moves energy from a producer to consumers. A food web is many chains joined. Decomposers return matter to the soil.  ·  Only about ten percent of the energy at one level is available at the next. The rest is lost as heat and as work of staying alive. Chains therefore stay short.  ·  A pond and a forest are both ecosystems. The pond's producers are algae and water plants. The forest's are trees. The structure differs. The energy rule does not.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Succession: gradual change in species composition over time (primary/secondary succession)  ·  Niche versus habitat.  ·  Food chain and web.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: About 10 percent energy transfer.  ·  A niche is not a habitat. The habitat is the address. The niche is the job.  ·  Decomposers are not producers.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Ecosystem services include pollination, water purification, and climate regulation.  ·  Order in a sequence is part of the answer.  ·  Do not call a timberline a snowline.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Energy flows through ecosystems but matter cycles continuously.  ·  Ecological succession describes how communities change over time after disturbance.  ·  Keystone species have disproportionately large effects on ecosystem structure.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Keystone species = has large impact relative to abundance.  ·  Give the character and one example.  ·  State the contrast.
